ambiguities.evidence: It says only that they are not necessarily given in u_low and then models conversion by fl_low. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: Theorem 3.2 and preceding conversion equations).
ambiguities.impact: The contract cannot add a hypothesis that the inputs are in u_high or any other fixed source format. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: Theorem 3.2).
ambiguities.issue: The theorem does not specify the original storage precision of A and B. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: Theorem 3.2).

ambiguities.evidence: Algorithm 3.1 separately assumes p=m/b_1, q=n/b, and r=t/b_2 are integers. (PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: Algorithm 3.1).
ambiguities.impact: Those conditions are inherited algorithmic context rather than additional words in the theorem statement. (PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: Theorem 3.2).
ambiguities.issue: Theorem 3.2 suppresses the outer block dimensions and their divisibility conditions. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: Theorem 3.2).

ambiguities.evidence: The paper says scaling might be necessary but then assumes underflow and overflow do not occur. (PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: paragraph following Algorithm 3.1).
ambiguities.impact: Equation (3.6) contains no scaling error or scale factor and should not be claimed for exceptional conversions without further assumptions. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: equation (3.6)).
ambiguities.issue: Scaling to avoid conversion underflow or overflow is mentioned but not analyzed. (PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: paragraph following Algorithm 3.1).

contract_plain_english: Algorithm 3.1 may first round arbitrary input matrices to u_low and then computes each output entry through q block FMAs. Theorem 3.2 combines both conversion errors with the chained-FMA error to give the exact componentwise coefficient in (3.6), including every squared and mixed term. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: conversion derivation, Theorem 3.2, and equation (3.6)).

source_evidence.anchor: standard floating-point model and gamma definitions
source_evidence.observation: The analysis uses gamma_k(v)=kv/(1-kv), accented gamma notation, and the standing assumption kv<1.

The matrix product is partitioned into compatible block sizes, operands are converted to u_low if necessary, q=n/b block products are accumulated with a block FMA, and the result is optionally rounded to output precision u.
The chained block-FMA error coefficient is tilde_gamma_q^FMA+bar_gamma_n+tilde_gamma_q^FMA bar_gamma_n.

For inputs not already in u_low, the paper models A_tilde=A+Delta A and B_tilde=B+Delta B with componentwise relative conversion bounds and expands the computed product into conversion and arithmetic errors.
The theorem states the componentwise error bound for arbitrary input matrices evaluated by Algorithm 3.1, retaining all conversion, gamma-product, and squared factors.

statement.algorithm_linkage: The result is specifically for Algorithm 3.1: low-precision operand conversion followed by q chained block FMAs for each output block and an optional final rounding to u. (PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: Theorem 3.2).
binders: Let A be in R^(m x n), B be in R^(n x t), and let the exact product be C=AB. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: Theorem 3.2).

Let b be the block inner dimension and q=n/b; Algorithm 3.1 additionally uses b_1 x b and b x b_2 blocks with p=m/b_1 and r=t/b_2 integral. (PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: Theorem 3.2).
Let C_hat be the matrix computed by Algorithm 3.1 after any required conversion of A and B to u_low. (PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: Theorem 3.2).

Let bar_u be the internal block-FMA unit roundoff, u_FMA its output unit roundoff, u the algorithm output unit roundoff, and tilde_u_FMA the effective rounding parameter from (3.3). (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equations (3.2) and (3.3)).
conclusions: |C-C_hat| <= [2u_low + u_low^2 + (tilde_gamma_q^FMA + bar_gamma_n + tilde_gamma_q^FMA bar_gamma_n)(1+u_low)^2] |A||B|, componentwise. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: equation (3.6)).
Before bounding, the computed result is decomposed as C_hat=AB+(Delta A)B+A(Delta B)+(Delta A)(Delta B)+Delta C=:AB+E. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: displayed decomposition preceding Theorem 3.2).

The theorem applies to the block-FMA Algorithm 3.1 and does not assert the standard-product bound (3.7), which is presented only for comparison. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: Theorem 3.2 and comparison equation (3.7)).
constants_and_indexing: q=n/b counts block-FMA accumulation steps, while n indexes the scalar internal-arithmetic gamma term. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.4); PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: equation (3.6)).
The conversion contribution is exactly 2u_low+u_low^2. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: equation (3.6)).
The arithmetic gamma coefficient is multiplied by (1+u_low)^2. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: equation (3.6)).
definitions_and_conventions: bar_gamma_k=k bar_u/(1-k bar_u), and tilde_gamma_k^FMA=k tilde_u_FMA/(1-k tilde_u_FMA). (PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor: gamma and accent definitions).
tilde_u_FMA is determined by the prioritized cases in (3.3), accounting for internal, FMA-output, and final-output precisions. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.3) and its clarification).

|A| and |B| are componentwise absolute-value matrices, while |A||B| is their ordinary matrix product. (PDF p. 3, printed C126, anchor: componentwise absolute-value convention; PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: equation (3.6)).
C denotes the exact real product and C_hat denotes the computed matrix. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)).
error_notions: Equation (3.6) is a componentwise absolute forward-error bound for a computed matrix product. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: equation (3.6)).
It is not a normwise bound and does not state a relative error for each nonzero entry of C. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: equation (3.6)).
exceptional_values: The initial conversions are explicitly assumed not to underflow or overflow. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: sentence before the conversion equations).
Algorithm 3.1's analysis likewise assumes no underflow or overflow; NaNs and infinities are not modeled. (PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: paragraph following Algorithm 3.1).
higher_order_terms: Equation (3.6) retains u_low^2, tilde_gamma_q^FMA bar_gamma_n, and the full square (1+u_low)^2. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: equation (3.6)).
No big-O term occurs in Theorem 3.2; the displayed coefficient is not merely its first-order part. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.6)).

The inherited chain analysis omits one of two possible successive output roundings and describes its effect as negligible rather than supplying an explicit remainder. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: double-rounding paragraph before (3.2)).
hypotheses: A and B need not initially be represented in precision u_low. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: Theorem 3.2).

If conversion is needed, A_tilde=fl_low(A)=A+Delta A and B_tilde=fl_low(B)=B+Delta B, with |Delta A|<=u_low|A| and |Delta B|<=u_low|B| componentwise. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: conversion equations preceding Theorem 3.2).
The conversion model assumes rounding without underflow or overflow. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: sentence introducing the conversion equations).

The block-FMA chain obeys the scalar bound (3.4), and all relevant gamma denominators are positive. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.4); PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor: gamma definition and standing assumption).
implicit_context: Theorem 3.2 names only q=n/b, while compatibility of b_1, b, and b_2 and integrality of p,q,r are inherited from Algorithm 3.1. (PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: Theorem 3.2).

The theorem leaves the original storage precision of A and B unspecified; it only says they are not necessarily in u_low and models their conversion. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: Theorem 3.2 and preceding conversion equations).

The output C is in precision u as specified by Algorithm 3.1, although u does not appear explicitly in (3.6) except through tilde_u_FMA. (PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.3)).
norms: No matrix norm is used; every absolute value is componentwise and the right-hand side contains the matrix product |A||B|. (PDF p. 3, printed C126, anchor: absolute-value convention; PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: equation (3.6)).
numerical_model: Initial conversions are one-rounding componentwise relative perturbations bounded by u_low. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: conversion equations before Theorem 3.2).
The block-product arithmetic contributes the exact coefficient tilde_gamma_q^FMA+bar_gamma_n+tilde_gamma_q^FMA bar_gamma_n from (3.4). (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.4)).
The underlying operations use the standard floating-point relative-error model. (PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor: equations (2.3) and (2.4)).

undebatable_constraints: A has shape m x n, B has shape n x t, and q=n/b. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: Theorem 3.2).
The inputs need not already be in u_low, so both initial conversion errors must be included. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: Theorem 3.2 and preceding conversion equations).
The bound is componentwise and multiplies |A||B|. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: equation (3.6)).
The complete coefficient is 2u_low+u_low^2+(tilde_gamma_q^FMA+bar_gamma_n+tilde_gamma_q^FMA bar_gamma_n)(1+u_low)^2. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: equation (3.6)).
None of the displayed second-order terms may be silently dropped. (PDF p. 7, printed C130, anchor: equation (3.6)).
